Design, Integration, and
Validation of a Modular
LLM-Based Interactive
Architecture
A NAO-centred ROS 2 architecture for grounded dialogue, structured planning, deterministic execution, and evidence-based reporting.
Juan David Bendek Williamson    •    Supervised by Raquel Ros    •    2025–2026

IIIA-CSIC / Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona
MSc Modelling for Science and Engineering
A plausible plan is not yet a safe robot action.

• Users refer to people, objects, and prior turns.

• One request can mix dialogue, knowledge, and action.

• A fluent plan can still omit targets or invent unsupported behaviour.

• Capabilities and arguments must be checked before dispatch.

• Identity, order, and lineage must survive execution.

• Completion must follow typed results and verified effects.
Example: “Bring all the objects you can see to ALEX.”
The study asks how flexibility can be integrated without surrendering execution control.

How can a modular robot architecture integrate dialogue, symbolic grounding, planning, deterministic execution, and feedback while preserving clear responsibility boundaries and evidence-based communication?
dialogue, grounding, planning, orchestration, and skills through explicit ROS 2 interfaces
candidate plans through reviewed capabilities and deterministic admission before dispatch
full turns, controlled failures, symbolic postconditions, and truthful reporting

Model-agnostic describes the interface boundary. Model-invariant would require equivalent behaviour, which the evidence did not show.

The model did not directly retry the robot. It proposed plan version 2 after receiving structured failure evidence.
It demonstrates middle-stage recovery, retained lineage, and a truthful closure. Beginning-stage navigation recovery was also retained; terminal recovery remained less reliable.

The strongest evidence concerns software contracts and symbolic state.

Another robot needs an equivalent reviewed skill registry and typed adapters. Another model must repeat the frozen qualification.
Controlled simulation reduced hardware variance and compute waste, but it cannot replace physical safety and performance measurement.

Quantify head and gaze behaviour, guarded wave, bounded local motion, semantic navigation, and pointing kinematics.
Evaluate detector identity settling and scene-grounding quality before promoting detector-derived facts into stronger claims.
Measure ASR, TTS, latency, interruption handling, and autonomous idle/request arbitration with users and physical trials.
Every promoted skill should begin with one physical success, one failure or cancellation, and the same typed evidence boundary.
The thesis contributes an architecture, a containment boundary, and a qualification method.
A modular ownership model connecting dialogue, grounding, planning, execution, and reporting.
Typed contracts and deterministic admission restrict model-generated execution authority.
A repeatable evidence method separates model, stack, observability, and physical claims.
Together, these boundaries make language-model variation observable without hiding task-level failure.

Language-model dialogue and planning can participate in an integrated robot architecture when their outputs are grounded, validated against reviewed skills, dispatched deterministically, and checked against typed feedback and symbolic postconditions.
The boundaries do not eliminate non-determinism. They make it observable and restrict its execution authority.

The thesis validates integration and containment, not a causal comparison of planning algorithms.
